headline: Claude Fable 5 jailbroken in 48 hours using layered evasion techniques
summary: Researchers bypassed Anthropic's safety measures with a combination of Unicode substitution, long-context framing, and narrative fiction.
details: Anthropic's Claude Fable 5, which underwent 1,000 hours of red-teaming, was reportedly jailbroken within 48 hours of its public release. A researcher known as Pliny the Liberator claimed to have bypassed the AI's guardrails using a layered approach.

The techniques employed included Unicode/homoglyph substitution, where standard characters are replaced with visually identical Unicode equivalents to evade detection. This was combined with long-context framing, burying harmful instructions deep within large amounts of text.

Narrative fiction framing, a long-standing jailbreak method, was also utilized by wrapping harmful requests in creative story contexts. Additionally, a decomposition-recomposition strategy broke down harmful requests into individually innocuous sub-prompts.

The claimed use cases for these jailbreaks were serious, including assistance with drug synthesis and attacks on cryptocurrency protocols. This highlights a structural problem with model-layer guardrails, which can be a single point of failure against determined researchers.

The effectiveness of these layered attacks stems from their ability to bypass intent classification at inference time. Each technique alone might be caught, but their combination creates enough surface area to exploit gaps in the AI's safety training.

While bug bounty programs are valuable, they test known techniques within a bounded timeframe and do not guarantee the absence of all possible evasion methods. A 1,000-hour bounty, while significant, did not prevent a rapid bypass.

To address such vulnerabilities, a system like Sentinel can be employed. It acts as a pre-model layer, analyzing input before the AI processes it. Sentinel normalizes text, resolves homoglyphs, and uses vector similarity to detect harmful content.

Sentinel's normalization layer strips invisible characters and maps homoglyphs to ASCII equivalents, ensuring that character substitutions are unwound before threat scanning. This prevents the model-layer guardrail from being blindsided by such tricks.

A fast-path regex layer then catches explicit authority hijack signatures and persona shift patterns. Finally, a deep-path vector similarity layer analyzes the semantic content of sub-prompts, even if they appear innocuous individually, comparing them against known attack signature embeddings.

headline: AI agent controls phone, sends real WhatsApp message offline
summary: A developer has created an AI agent capable of controlling a smartphone to send messages via WhatsApp without an internet connection, marking a significant step in mobile AI autonomy.
details: A new AI agent has demonstrated the ability to fully control a smartphone, including sending messages through apps like WhatsApp. The agent successfully opened the app, selected a contact, composed a message, and sent it, all without requiring an internet connection.

This breakthrough was achieved through step-by-step verification and is detailed in a GitHub repository, showcasing the agent's offline capabilities. The project highlights the potential for AI to operate autonomously on mobile devices.

The developer behind the project shared the progress on Day 4 of building the AI agent, emphasizing the verified, offline nature of the WhatsApp message sending. This development could pave the way for more sophisticated mobile AI applications that function independently of network connectivity.
